title: LD pruning

blocks.what_we_do: We select a smaller set of [autosomal](docs/glossary.md#autosome) variants that are less correlated with each other. Removing correlated variants is called pruning for [linkage disequilibrium](docs/glossary.md#ld) (LD). Autosomes are the chromosomes 1 to 22. We use this set for the heterozygosity check, for the relatedness check and, later, for [principal component analysis](docs/glossary.md#pca-pc) (PCA). PCA is a method that summarises the genetic differences between people.
blocks.why:
[Linkage disequilibrium](docs/glossary.md#ld) (LD) means that alleles at nearby sites are correlated. A dense region with many correlated sites would count too much, only because the array has many [probes](docs/glossary.md#probe) there. A probe is the piece of DNA on the array that measures one site.

[LD pruning](docs/glossary.md#ld-pruning) keeps one representative subset of sites. It does not delete the other sites from the association data.

We also leave out the long-range LD regions, where the correlation reaches over very long distances. These regions are known to pull principal components towards themselves. Examples are the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) on chromosome 6, the 8p23 inversion on chromosome 8 and the 17q21 inversion on chromosome 17.

The course uses a list of 18 regions on build GRCh38. It collects the regions that were published for genome scans and for principal component analysis (Price et al. 2008, doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2008.06.005; Anderson et al. 2010, doi:10.1038/nprot.2010.116; Privé et al. 2020, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa520). The regions follow the list collected by Grinde et al. 2024 ([doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1011242](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1011242)). Nine regions that sit around centromeres could not be converted from build 36 to GRCh38, so the list does not contain them. The list is a BED file in the course data (`pca_reference/highLD_b38.bed`), not in the project. It is not a complete catalogue for all studies.
blocks.command:
```{r s3-4}
# 1. Write the list of regions where nearby variants are strongly correlated.
regions <- guided_high_ld(cfg)
# 2. Select variants with less similar patterns of DNA letters.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), "--chr", "1-22", "--maf", "0.05", "--geno", "0.02",
  "--exclude", "bed0", regions, "--indep-pairwise", "200kb", "0.2", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune")))
# 3. Check and print how many variants were selected.
pruned <- readLines(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), ".prune.in"))
stopifnot(length(pruned) == 68800L)
cat(length(pruned), "variants kept by LD pruning\n")
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "3.4", c(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), c(".prune.in", ".prune.out")), regions), parent = "3.3")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --chr 1-22 --maf 0.05 --geno 0.02 --exclude bed0 results/guided/s3-4_high_ld.bed0 --indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2 --out results/guided/s3-4_prune --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--chr 1-22` keeps only the autosomes. `--maf 0.05` keeps common variants, which means a [minor allele frequency](docs/glossary.md#maf) (MAF) of at least 5%. `--geno 0.02` removes variants with more than 2% missing genotypes, so this subset has a variant call rate of at least 98%. `--exclude bed0` leaves out the sites inside the listed regions. The file is a BED file: it gives each region as a chromosome, a start counted from 0 and an end that is not included. `--indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2` prunes within windows of 200 kb (200,000 base pairs of DNA), with a limit of 0.2 for the squared correlation, called [r^2](docs/glossary.md#r-squared). `--out`, `--threads` and `--memory` have the meanings given at step 3.1.

The `.prune.in` file lists 68,800 sites. The complete analysis state still has 296,360 variants.

blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file named in the message and the previous step. Keep the command and the console messages. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: Regions that would otherwise dominate summaries made from correlated markers. The subset that you keep depends on the input samples and on the exact version of the algorithm.
blocks.quick_check:
Should the later association scan test only the pruned sites?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. We use pruning only for specific checks and for the PCA. The association scan uses the full set of variants that pass quality control (QC).

</details>
blocks.try_other_thresholds:
This optional box is not part of the main path and does not change your results. The examples use simulated data, so the true answer is known ([why](lessons/module_05_population_structure.Rmd#step-5-1)).

Each trial changes one setting of LD pruning. Here "removed" means pruned out.

**Chart: r2 limit.**

**Why this simulation.** LD pruning drops one variant of each correlated pair. How strict should the correlation limit be?

**How to read the chart.** Each point is one r2 limit, the squared correlation above which one variant of a pair is dropped. The vertical axis counts the variants pruned out, and the diamond marks the course value.

**Try this.**

- Move the slider to **0.1**. More variants are dropped.
- Move it to **0.5**. Fewer variants are dropped.

**What you should see, and why.** A low limit counts weaker correlations as pairs, so it drops more variants. A high limit keeps pairs of similar variants, which then count twice in the PCA.

**Why it matters for your GWAS.** [step 3.4](lessons/module_03_sample_quality_control.Rmd#step-3-4) makes the variant list that the next checks and the PCA use. Too many correlated variants overweight some regions, and too few lose information.

**Key idea:** Pruning trades independence against information, and the course takes a middle value.

**Chart: window (kb).**

**Why this simulation.** The window is how far apart two variants may be and still be compared. Does it matter as much?

**How to read the chart.** Each point is one window length in kb. The axes and the diamond are as above.

**Try this.**

- Move the slider to **50**. Note the count.
- Move it to **1000**. The count changes less than it did for the r2 limit.

**What you should see, and why.** A wider window finds more pairs, but the count changes much less than for the r2 limit, because correlation fades with distance.

**Why it matters for your GWAS.** In [step 3.4](lessons/module_03_sample_quality_control.Rmd#step-3-4) you can keep the course window. The r2 limit is the setting that decides how many variants you keep.

**Key idea:** The window matters less than the r2 limit.

```{r s3-4_thresholds, eval=FALSE}
# Course check. This step needs project version 2026.5 or later.
if (!exists("requires_course_version")) stop("This step needs project version 2026.5 or later. Your project is older. Download the new version at step 0.3.", call. = FALSE)
requires_course_version("2026.5")
# Optional. Each trial starts from the same input and changes one setting only. It writes no file in your results folder.
regions <- guided_high_ld(cfg)
# 1. Change the r2 limit, with a window of 200 kb.
r2_limits <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5)
by_r2 <- sapply(r2_limits, function(r) prune_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), regions, r2 = r, window_kb = 200))
# 2. Change the window, with an r2 limit of 0.2.
windows <- c(50, 200, 1000)
by_window <- sapply(windows, function(w) prune_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), regions, r2 = 0.2, window_kb = w))
data.frame(r2 = r2_limits, kept = by_r2["kept", ], pruned = by_r2["pruned", ])
data.frame(window_kb = windows, kept = by_window["kept", ], pruned = by_window["pruned", ])
# 3. Plot the pruned variants. The course value is the large diamond.
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot_threshold_trials(data.frame(threshold = r2_limits, removed = by_r2["pruned", ], course_value = r2_limits == 0.2), "Variants pruned out", log_x = FALSE)
plot_threshold_trials(data.frame(threshold = windows, removed = by_window["pruned", ], course_value = windows == 200), "Variants pruned out")
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```
Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --chr 1-22 --maf 0.05 --geno 0.02 --exclude bed0 results/guided/s3-4_high_ld.bed0 --indep-pairwise 200kb 0.5 --out results/trials/s3-4_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

Count the lines of `results/trials/s3-4_trial.prune.in`: it is the number of variants kept.

The expected result of the trials:

Variants pruned out and kept when the r^2 limit changes (window 200 kb):

| Setting | Variants removed | Variants remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.1 | 76,459 | 48,602 |
| **0.2 (course value)** | 56,261 | 68,800 |
| 0.5 | 24,308 | 100,753 |

Variants pruned out and kept when the window changes (r^2 limit 0.2):

| Setting | Variants removed | Variants remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 50 | 46,961 | 78,100 |
| **200 (course value)** | 56,261 | 68,800 |
| 1000 | 57,375 | 67,686 |
blocks.deep_dive:
This optional box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it.

#### Deep dive: what happens if the long-range LD regions stay in?

**The idea.** A principal component should describe differences between people across the whole genome. In a region with a long stretch of strongly correlated variants, one pattern repeats over thousands of sites. A PC can then describe that one region instead of the ancestry of the people. This is why this step leaves such regions out before the PCA.

**Where to see it.** You cannot see this effect yet, because the PCs are calculated in module 5. The optional deep dive "Can one region take over a PC?" in step 5.7 does the experiment on your own data. It calculates the PCs with and without the list of regions, and it plots the loadings along the genome. A loading tells how much a variant contributes to a PC.

**Quick check.** Why do we leave the regions out before the PCA, and not only before the association scan?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The regions disturb the PCs, and the PCs are then used as covariates in the scan. The association scan itself still uses all the variants that pass quality control.

</details>

**Reference.** Price et al. 2008 ([doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2008.06.005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajhg.2008.06.005)) describe long-range LD that can confound genome scans in admixed populations. Privé et al. 2020 ([doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa520](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa520)) report that some PCs capture LD structure and not population structure.
blocks.under_the_hood:
**What the tool computes.** `--indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2` moves a 200 kb window along each chromosome one variant at a time. In each window it calculates r^2, the squared correlation between the genotype counts (0, 1 or 2) of two variants, from unphased hard calls. For every pair above 0.2 it drops one of the two. `.prune.in` lists the kept variants and `.prune.out` the dropped ones. No genotype is deleted.

**Why these values.** The window, the limit of 0.2 and the 5% frequency filter are conventions, not laws. A looser limit such as 0.5 keeps more variants. Windows counted in variants, with a step above 1, are also widely used. Here the filter leaves 68,800 sites, enough for the checks that follow.

**Pitfalls.** Some regions, such as the HLA region on chromosome 6, are correlated over very long distances. Pruning thins them but does not remove their pull on principal components, so the course excludes listed regions first. The list belongs to one genome build and is not complete. In this dataset, the list excludes about 9,500 array variants (before the frequency and call-rate filters), compared with about 5,700 for the short list that earlier versions of the course used. The pruned set also depends on the samples, the frequency filter and the scan order, so another cohort gives another list. Never use it for the association scan.

**References**

1. Price AL et al. (2008) Long-range LD can confound genome scans in admixed populations. Am J Hum Genet 83:132-135. PMID 18606306.
2. Anderson CA et al. (2010) Data quality control in genetic case-control association studies. Nat Protoc 5:1564-1573. PMID 21085122.
3. Privé F et al. (2020) Efficient toolkit implementing best practices for principal component analysis of population genetic data. Bioinformatics 36:4449-4457. PMID 32415959.
4. Chang CC et al. (2015) Second-generation PLINK: rising to the challenge of larger and richer datasets. GigaScience 4:7. PMID 25722852.

options.name: --exclude
options.explanation_markdown: `--exclude bed0` leaves out the sites inside the listed regions.

options.name: --geno
options.explanation_markdown: `--geno 0.02` removes variants with more than 2% missing genotypes, so this subset has a variant call rate of at least 98%.

options.name: --indep-pairwise
options.explanation_markdown: `--indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2` prunes within windows of 200 kb (200,000 base pairs of DNA), with a limit of 0.2 for the squared correlation, called [r^2](docs/glossary.md#r-squared).

options.name: --maf

options.name: --memory

options.name: --out
options.explanation_markdown: `--out` sets the name prefix of the output files.

options.name: --pfile

options.name: --threads
options.explanation_markdown: `--threads 2` limits the number of worker threads (parallel jobs).

student_summary: We select common DNA sites that are less strongly correlated with each other. This stops groups of similar sites from weighing too much in the sample checks. The full dataset is kept for the association scan.

options.name: --pfile
options.explanation: Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix.

options.name: --chr
options.explanation: Uses only chromosomes 1 to 22, the autosomes.

options.name: --maf
options.explanation: Keeps variants whose less common allele has a frequency of at least 5%.

options.name: --geno
options.explanation: Keeps variants with no more than 2% missing calls.

options.name: --exclude
options.explanation: Leaves out variants within the listed DNA regions.

modifiers.name: bed0
modifiers.explanation: Reads DNA regions in the BED way: the start of each region is counted from 0 and its end is not included.

options.name: --indep-pairwise
options.explanation: Compares genotype patterns at pairs of sites within windows of 200 kb (200,000 DNA bases). It drops one site of every pair with a squared correlation (r²) above 0.2. A larger r² means that the genotypes of the two sites vary together more closely.

options.name: --out
options.explanation: Sets the shared beginning of the output file names.
